docs.title: valheim-server-improved
docs.text:
valheim-server-improved is a ready-to-run Docker Compose setup for the community-valheim-tools/valheim-server image. It uses that image unchanged and improves the setup around it:

  • The server runs as your user, not root, and only the ports you need are open.
  • A healthcheck reports healthy once the game is listening, and container logs are capped at about 30 MB.
  • restart.sh refuses to start with the example password or one the server would reject.
  • Wipes archive everything first and keep your admins; restores are documented.
  • Discord notifications are built in and stay off until you turn them on.
  • It can stop the server while nobody plays and start it on the next connection attempt. This is also off until you turn it on.

Improvements over Upstream compares it with the upstream example point by point. To get started, see the Quick Start.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Linux host with Docker Engine and the compose plugin, and a user in the docker group to run the scripts.
  • About 4 GB of disk for the game server files.
  • UDP ports 2456–2457 forwarded to the host. See Players, Admins and Bans.
  • CPU and memory for your player count:
Players online CPU Memory 1–5 2 fast vCPUs 4 GB 6–10 4 fast vCPUs 6–8 GB Modded 4 fast vCPUs to start 8 GB to start

Vanilla Valheim allows at most 10 players at once. Most of the server's CPU load runs on one thread, so a few fast cores beat many slow ones. These figures are starting points based on Supercraft's hosting data; Iron Gate publishes no server requirements. Check docker stats during a busy session.

docs.title: Container Limits
docs.text: By default, docker-compose.yml caps the container at 8 GB of memory, reserves 4 GB, and leaves CPU unlimited. To change this, edit deploy.resources; to remove the limits, delete the deploy: block.

docs.title: Improvements over Upstream
docs.text:
valheim-server-improved runs the community-valheim-tools/valheim-server image unchanged. The game server, the update and backup services, and the image's settings all come from upstream. What differs is the Compose file, the defaults in env/valheim.env.example, the helper scripts and the documentation.

Comparisons below are against upstream's docker-compose.yaml and the image's defaults file.

docs.title: Safer Defaults
docs.text: Upstream This setup User the server runs as root (PUID=0, PGID=0) Your user (PUID=1000, PGID=1000), so files on the host are yours Supervisor web UI port 9001 Published on every interface, although the UI is off by default Not published Crossplay port 2458/udp Always published Published only if you uncomment it for CROSSPLAY=true Status page Not published Published on 127.0.0.1 only Restart policy always: a stopped server comes back after a reboot unless-stopped: a stopped server stays stopped Password check The server fails to start, and the reason is in the log restart.sh refuses to start with the example password, one under 5 characters, or one inside the server name

docs.title: Fewer Ways to Lose Data
docs.text:
• Wipes archive first. wipe-restart.sh asks you to type the world name, checks it can delete everything before it deletes anything, then saves data/ and backups/ to a .tar.gz in wipe-archives/.
  • Wipes keep your admins. The admin, ban and permitted lists survive a wipe.
  • Restores are documented. Backups and Wipes has step-by-step restores from an hourly backup and from a wipe archive. Upstream documents none.
  • Idle hours don't push out real backups. BACKUPS_IF_IDLE=false stops backups an hour after the last player leaves. The image's default (true) keeps backing up while nobody plays, so with a 12-backup limit, one idle night replaces every backup of the last session. At each restart, hooks/idle-backups.sh also deletes the previous backup if nobody has played since it, so restarts don't pile up backups of idle time.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Upstream This setup Healthcheck None healthy once the game is listening, from the image's own status file. Works on private servers too. Container logs Unlimited At most about 30 MB (3 × 10 MB) Memory No limits 4 GB reserved, 8 GB cap, with sizing guidance by player count Paths Fixed to $HOME/valheim-server Relative to the repository, so it runs from any folder Day-to-day commands docker compose by hand restart.sh, stop.sh, logs.sh, wipe-restart.sh restart.sh — Pulls the image and always restarts, even when nothing changed Idle servers Always running Optional sleep when idle: stops the server when nobody plays and starts it on the next connection attempt Backup history Every container start adds a backup, so restarts push out older ones Backups taken while nobody played replace each other instead of piling up Notifications Hand-written curl commands in hook variables, with quoting examples per shell Discord notifications built in and off by default: set a webhook and list the events. Messages are JSON-escaped, and player names can't ping @everyone. Other services plug in as adapters.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Admins, bans and the whitelist, including that ADMINLIST_IDS replaces the file's contents.
  • Resource sizing by player count.
  • How players join, and the ports to forward.
  • A pointer to the image's undocumented variables in its defaults file.

docs.title: What Is Not Different
docs.text:
• Performance. Same image, same game server. Nothing here makes it faster.
  • Features. Mods, hooks, crossplay and everything else come from the image. Its README remains the full reference.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Clone the repository and run every command from its root:

git clone https://github.com/JacobSanford/valheim-server-improved.git
cd valheim-server-improved

docs.title: Copy the Settings
docs.text:
The copy holds the server password, so make it readable only by you:

cp env/valheim.env.example env/valheim.env
chmod 600 env/valheim.env

docs.title: Set the Password and User
docs.text:
In env/valheim.env:

  1. Replace SERVER_PASS=changeme with your own password. It must be at least 5 characters and must not appear in SERVER_NAME. The game server rejects both, and restart.sh checks them before starting.
  2. The server runs as PUID/PGID and writes data/ and backups/ as that user. If id -u or id -g prints a number other than 1000, set the matching variable to that number.

Every other setting is in the Reference.

docs.title: Start the Server
docs.text:
./restart.sh

The script checks the password, starts the server, then follows the logs. Press Ctrl+C to leave them; the server keeps running. The first start takes longer, because it downloads the game server files.

The server is ready when the log shows Game server connected, and docker compose ps shows the container as healthy.

Next, let players join.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set in env/valheim.env. Values shown are those in env/valheim.env.example.

Variable Value Meaning SERVER_NAME My Valheim Server The name shown in the server browser. WORLD_NAME Dedicated The world save to load. If no save has this name, a new world is created. SERVER_PASS changeme The password players enter to join. At least 5 characters, and not part of the server name. SERVER_PORT 2456 The game port. The server also uses the next port (2457). Changing it also needs the ports: mapping in docker-compose.yml changed to match. SERVER_PUBLIC true Lists the server in the public server browser. CROSSPLAY false Allows Xbox, Microsoft Store and Apple App Store players to join. TZ Etc/UTC The timezone used for logs and the cron schedules below. PUID / PGID 1000 The user and group the server runs as, and that own the files on the host. The image's default is 0 (root). BACKUPS true Saves a backup of the world to backups/ at 5 minutes past each hour. BACKUPS_MAX_AGE 30 Deletes backups older than this many days. BACKUPS_MAX_COUNT 12 Keeps at most this many backups. BACKUPS_IF_IDLE false Stops backing up an hour after the last player leaves. UPDATE_CRON */15 * * * * How often to check for game updates, as a cron schedule. UPDATE_IF_IDLE true Applies an update only when no players are online. RESTART_CRON 10 5 * * * Restarts the server every day at 5:10 AM. RESTART_IF_IDLE true Skips the daily restart if any players are online. STATUS_HTTP true Serves server status at http://127.0.0.1:8456/status.json, reachable only from the host. Reports the server only while SERVER_PUBLIC=true. ADMINLIST_IDS unset Admins, as platform IDs such as Steam_<STEAMID64>, separated by spaces. Replaces data/adminlist.txt. BANNEDLIST_IDS unset Banned players. Replaces data/bannedlist.txt. PERMITTEDLIST_IDS unset The only players allowed to join. Replaces data/permittedlist.txt. NOTIFY_EVENTS empty Notification events to send, comma separated, or all. Empty sends nothing. NOTIFY_DISCORD_WEBHOOK empty Discord webhook URL. Empty turns the Discord adapter off. NOTIFY_DISCORD_USERNAME unset The name messages are posted under. Defaults to SERVER_NAME. SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE false Stops the server when nobody is playing and starts it on the next connection attempt. See Sleep When Idle. SLEEP_METHOD stop stop frees the memory; pause keeps it and wakes in about 5 seconds. SLEEP_AFTER_SECONDS 1200 How far back packets are counted, and how long that count must stay below SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS before sleeping, in seconds. 300 to 65535. SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS 10 Packets on ports 2456–2457 within SLEEP_AFTER_SECONDS that count as activity and wake the server.

The env example also sets the image's event hooks and two log filters, to feed notifications and the backup pruning in hooks/idle-backups.sh. See Discord Notifications and Backups and Wipes.

The image's README lists every documented option, including those not set here. A few more are undocumented; they are listed with their defaults in the image's defaults file.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run from the repository root.

Script Does restart.sh Checks SERVER_PASS, pulls the latest image, starts or restarts the server, then follows the last 200 log lines. Restarting disconnects players. stop.sh Stops the server and removes the container. The world is kept. logs.sh Follows the server logs, starting from the last 200 lines. notify-test.sh Sends a test notification from the running server. wipe-restart.sh Archives data/ and backups/, deletes every saved world (not only WORLD_NAME) and all backups, keeps the player lists, and starts a new world. lib.sh Helpers the other scripts share. Not run directly.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Port Purpose Published 2456–2457/udp Game and query ports On every interface 2458/udp Crossplay Only if uncommented in docker-compose.yml 8456/tcp Status page (status.json) On 127.0.0.1 only

With SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=true, these ports are published by the lazytainer container (Lazytainer) in docker-compose.sleep.yml instead, and Valheim shares its network. For crossplay, uncomment the 2458:2458/udp line there too.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Path Contents In git data/ World saves and the admin, ban and permitted lists. Mounted in the container as /config. No server/ The game server files (about 4 GB), downloaded automatically. No backups/ The hourly world backups. No wipe-archives/ Archives saved by wipe-restart.sh and by restores. No env/valheim.env Your settings, including the server password and webhook. No notify/ The notification script and its adapters. Mounted read-only as /opt/notify. Yes hooks/ idle-backups.sh, which prunes backups taken while nobody plays. Mounted read-only as /opt/hooks. Yes docker-compose.sleep.yml Added on top of docker-compose.yml by the scripts when SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=true. Yes data/.player-activity Touched when a player spawns, and every 10 minutes while players are online. idle-backups.sh uses its date. No

docs.title: restart.sh Refuses to Start
docs.text:
It checks env/valheim.env before starting and names the problem:

Message Fix env/valheim.env not found Copy the example. See the Quick Start. SERVER_PASS ... is still the example value Set your own password. SERVER_PASS ... must be at least 5 characters Use a longer password. SERVER_PASS must not appear in SERVER_NAME Change one of them.

docs.title: The Server Stays Unhealthy
docs.text:
If docker compose ps shows unhealthy, or still shows health: starting a few minutes after the download finishes, read the log with ./logs.sh. The healthcheck allows the first start 15 minutes for the download. With SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=true, unhealthy is also expected while the server sleeps; see Sleep When Idle.

If the log shows Steamcmd needs to be online to update, the container can't reach the internet, so it can't download the game. Check from inside the container:

docker compose exec valheim curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.steampowered.com/

Any HTTP status, such as 404, means it can connect. A timeout means something on the host blocks traffic from Docker networks, such as a VPN client or a firewall that only allows Docker's default bridge.

docs.title: The Server Doesn't Wake
docs.text: With SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=true, a join attempt has to send more than SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS packets to ports 2456–2457 to wake the server. Lower SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS and run ./restart.sh. Players must use Join IP, because a sleeping server isn't in the Community list. See Sleep When Idle.

docs.title: The Status Page Shows an Error
docs.text: status.json reports error until the server answers status queries, so expect one for the first minute. It reports the server only while SERVER_PUBLIC=true, so for a private server, use docker compose ps instead.

docs.title: wipe-restart.sh Says a Folder Is Not Writable
docs.text:
Some files under data/ or backups/ belong to another user, often root from a run without PUID/PGID. Nothing was deleted. Take ownership, then run the wipe again:

sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" data backups

docs.title: Notifications Don't Arrive
docs.text:
Run ./notify-test.sh. It prints the reason a send failed:

Output Fix notify: no adapter is configured Set NOTIFY_DISCORD_WEBHOOK in env/valheim.env and run ./restart.sh. discord: HTTP 401 or HTTP 404, Invalid Webhook Token or Unknown Webhook The webhook URL is wrong or the webhook was deleted. Copy it again from Discord. Could not resolve host The container can't reach the internet. See The Server Stays Unhealthy.

If the test arrives but events don't, check the event is listed in NOTIFY_EVENTS and the hook lines from env/valheim.env.example are in your env/valheim.env.

docs.title: Backups and Wipes
docs.text:
The server writes a backup of the world to backups/ each time the container starts and at 5 minutes past each hour, keeping at most 12 and none older than 30 days. Backups stop an hour after the last player leaves.

A running server saves the world even when nobody is on, so every restart adds a backup that differs from the last one only by idle time. When nobody has played since the previous backup, hooks/idle-backups.sh deletes that previous one and keeps the new one, so restarts and idle hours can't push out backups of real play.

Run every command from the repository root, and replace the placeholders:

Placeholder Replace with <WORLD_NAME> The WORLD_NAME value in env/valheim.env <YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS> The timestamp in the name of the backup or archive you are restoring

docs.title: Restore an Hourly Backup
docs.text:
Each file in backups/ is a zip of the world, named worlds-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.zip. The current world is moved to wipe-archives/, not deleted. The commands need unzip installed on the host.

./stop.sh
mkdir -p restore-tmp wipe-archives
unzip -q backups/worlds-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.zip -d restore-tmp
mv "data/worlds_local/<WORLD_NAME>" "wipe-archives/<WORLD_NAME>-before-restore-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mv "restore-tmp/config/worlds_local/<WORLD_NAME>" "data/worlds_local/<WORLD_NAME>"
rm -r restore-tmp
./restart.sh

docs.title: Wipe the World
docs.text:
wipe-restart.sh deletes every world, not only <WORLD_NAME>: everything in data/worlds_local/, in data/worlds/ if present, and in backups/. It keeps the admin, ban and permitted lists. Before deleting, it asks you to type the world name, checks it can delete everything, and saves data/ and backups/ to wipe-archives/<WORLD_NAME>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz. It then starts a new world.

./wipe-restart.sh

docs.title: Restore a Wipe Archive
docs.text:
A wipe archive holds data/ and backups/ as they were before the wipe. Restoring it deletes everything in data/, including the current world and the player lists, without archiving them first. The old world's backups return to backups/, beside any made since the wipe.

./stop.sh
rm -rf data/*
tar -xzf "wipe-archives/<WORLD_NAME>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz"
./restart.sh

After any restore, check the log shows Game server connected.

docs.title: Discord Notifications
docs.text: Notifications are off until you turn them on.

docs.title: Turn Them On
docs.text:
1. In Discord, open Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks, create a webhook for the channel you want, and copy its URL. Discord's Intro to Webhooks shows the steps.

  2. In env/valheim.env, set the webhook and list the events you want, comma separated:

    NOTIFY_EVENTS=server_up,server_down,player_spawned
NOTIFY_DISCORD_WEBHOOK=https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...

  3. Run ./restart.sh, then press Ctrl+C to leave the log view. The server keeps running.

  4. Run ./notify-test.sh. It sends a test message whatever NOTIFY_EVENTS says. On success it prints notify: discord: sent; on failure it prints the reason, for example discord: HTTP 401: Invalid Webhook Token, and exits non-zero.

The webhook URL lets anyone post to your channel. Keep it in env/valheim.env, which git ignores and only you can read.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event Sent when server_up The server starts accepting connections. server_down The server begins shutting down. restart The server restarts to apply a game update. The daily RESTART_CRON restart sends server_down and server_up instead. backup A world backup is written. See Backups and Wipes for when. Not sent when the backup replaced an idle one. player_spawned A player spawns into the world, including after a death.

NOTIFY_EVENTS=all turns on every event. Messages are posted under the server's name; set NOTIFY_DISCORD_USERNAME to change it (Discord rejects names containing "discord").

docs.title: When Sending Fails
docs.text: The server carries on. The reason goes to the container log (./logs.sh), with the HTTP status and Discord's reason but never the webhook URL. Each attempt gives up after 10 seconds, and failed messages are not retried.

docs.title: Keep Your Own Hook Commands
docs.text:
The env example connects the image's event hooks, such as POST_SERVER_LISTENING_HOOK, to notify/notify.sh. Keep those lines when you copy settings across. To run your own command on the same event, append it after a ;, in place of <YOUR_COMMAND>:

PRE_RESTART_HOOK=/opt/notify/notify.sh restart; <YOUR_COMMAND>

docs.title: Add Another Service
docs.text:
Each service is an adapter: a file in notify/adapters/ that defines two functions.

Function Does adapter_enabled Exits 0 if the adapter is configured, usually because its webhook variable is set. adapter_send EVENT MESSAGE Delivers MESSAGE. Exits non-zero on failure, with the reason on stderr.

notify/adapters/discord.sh is the example. notify.sh runs every enabled adapter for each event, so Discord and a new service can both be on at once.

docs.title: Forward the Ports
docs.text: Forward UDP ports 2456–2457 to the host. With CROSSPLAY=true, also forward UDP 2458, uncomment the 2458:2458/udp line in docker-compose.yml, and run ./restart.sh.

docs.title: Join from the Game
docs.text:
Players join in one of two ways, then enter the server password:

  • Join Game → Community. The list loads only 200 servers at a time, so type part of your SERVER_NAME in the filter. The server is listed only while SERVER_PUBLIC=true.
  • Join Game → Join IP, then enter the host's public IP address or hostname. Port 2456 is the default and can be left off. This works even when SERVER_PUBLIC=false.

docs.title: Manage Admins, Bans and the Whitelist
docs.text:
The lists are adminlist.txt, bannedlist.txt and permittedlist.txt in data/. When the permitted list has entries, only those players can join. Each entry is a platform user ID, such as Steam_<STEAMID64>, and is case sensitive, according to Iron Gate's server manual (server/server/Valheim Dedicated Server Manual.pdf, downloaded with the game server files). A player finds theirs in the F2 panel in game; it also appears in the server log when they connect.

Manage each list one of two ways, not both:

  • Set ADMINLIST_IDS, BANNEDLIST_IDS or PERMITTEDLIST_IDS in env/valheim.env as IDs separated by spaces, then run ./restart.sh. A non-empty variable replaces everything in the matching file.
  • Leave the variable unset and edit the file in data/, one ID per line, then run ./restart.sh.

The lists survive a wipe.

docs.title: Sleep When Idle
docs.text: Sleep when idle is off by default. When it's on, a small extra container, Lazytainer, takes over ports 2456–2457 and counts the packets on them. Lazytainer counts the packets of the last 20 minutes. Once that count has stayed under 10 for another 20 minutes, it stops the server, about 40 minutes after the last player leaves. When more than 10 arrive within 20 minutes, it starts the server again.

docs.title: Before You Turn It On
docs.text:
• Lazytainer controls Docker. It needs the Docker socket to start and stop the server, and read-only mounting doesn't limit what the socket can do. Anyone who takes over that container controls the host; see Docker's security notes on the daemon's attack surface.

  • A public server may never sleep. Server browsers and internet scans also send packets to the game ports. If they reach the threshold, the server stays awake. This hasn't been tested on a server reachable from the internet. If the idle count in ./logs.sh keeps resetting before it reaches SLEEP_AFTER_SECONDS, raise SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS, or set SERVER_PUBLIC=false so the server isn't listed in the server browser.

  • Crossplay needs its port in the sleep file too. The sleep file replaces the Valheim container's ports, and its 2458:2458/udp line is commented out. With CROSSPLAY=true, uncomment it in docker-compose.sleep.yml as well. Lazytainer counts only ports 2456–2457.

  • Docker Compose 2.18 or later. The sleep file uses Compose's !reset tag, which older versions reject.

docs.title: Turn It On
docs.text:
1. In env/valheim.env, set:

    SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=true

  2. Run ./restart.sh, then press Ctrl+C to leave the log view.

./logs.sh now also shows Lazytainer counting idle time, for example 300 / 1200 seconds without an active client or sufficient traffic on running container. While the server sleeps, docker compose ps -a shows it as exited (stop) or paused. Plain docker compose ps leaves out a stopped server. Its health reads unhealthy until it wakes; that's expected.

The scripts add docker-compose.sleep.yml for you and pass it the SLEEP_ settings from env/valheim.env. To run docker compose yourself, add the file too, as below. Start the server with ./restart.sh, though: a hand-run docker compose up doesn't read those settings and uses the defaults.

COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker-compose.sleep.yml docker compose ps -a

docs.title: What Players See
docs.text:
While the server sleeps, it isn't in the Community list, so players join with Join IP. Their first attempt should wake the server; this hasn't been tested with the game itself.

The wake times were measured with a private test server and small world: from the first packet to healthy took 30–36 seconds when stopped, and the paused server was running again 6 seconds after it. A game update at wake adds its download time. How many packets a real join attempt sends wasn't measured; if one doesn't wake the server, lower SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS.

SLEEP_METHOD Memory while asleep Wake First join attempt (expected) stop (default) Freed About 35 seconds Times out; join again once the server is up pause Kept About 5 seconds May time out; a second attempt gets in

docs.title: How Sleeping Changes Updates and Backups
docs.text:
stop pause Game updates Checked at every wake, which takes longer when there is one Checked only while awake. The 40 minutes or so before sleeping are longer than the 15-minute update interval, so each sleep follows an update check Backups Every wake writes one. When nobody has played since the previous backup, that one is deleted, so wakes don't pile up backups None while paused Daily restart Not needed: every wake is a fresh start Skipped if the server is paused at 5:10 AM World save Saved every time it sleeps Not saved: if the host reboots while paused, play since the last autosave is lost Notifications server_down at every sleep, server_up at every wake None

The image deletes backups older than BACKUPS_MAX_AGE at each backup, including the one at wake. The env example sets BACKUPS_MAX_AGE=30; the image's own default is 3. With 30, a wake after weeks asleep still keeps the last backups, but after more than 30 days asleep only the wake's own backup is left. Raise BACKUPS_MAX_AGE if the server may sleep longer.

docs.title: Tune It
docs.text:
Setting Default Change it when SLEEP_AFTER_SECONDS 1200 You want it to sleep sooner or later. Keep it above 900, so an update check runs before each sleep. The scripts refuse less than 300, because a wake must finish first. SLEEP_MIN_PACKETS 10 Scans or browser queries keep waking it or keep it awake: raise it. A join attempt doesn't wake it: lower it.

Run ./restart.sh after changing either.

To turn sleeping off, set SLEEP_WHEN_IDLE=false and run ./restart.sh. It removes the Lazytainer container and publishes the ports from the Valheim container again.
